evals.name: read-only-complexity-pass
evals.prompt: This service repo grew fast over the last month and I think it has duplicated config loaders and a couple of layers nobody needs. Do a read-only complexity pass: what would you look for, how would you rank what to simplify first, and what would you refuse to remove on name or age alone? Don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Selects the complexity lens for a report-only sweep, pins the inspected revision, traces consumers before calling anything unused, and ranks findings by drift and maintenance saved against migration cost.
assertions: Keeps the pass report-only: it makes no edits, commits or PRs itself. Recommending simplifications as findings for later approval is expected and does not count as planning edits.
Before calling a path unused, traces its callers and consumers, including dynamic, deployed or other-repository consumers, and says an empty local search is not proof.
Ranks findings by repeated drift, change frequency or maintenance saved against migration effort, uncertainty or blast radius.
Says age or naming alone never justify removing something.

evals.name: legacy-and-diagnostics-cleanup
evals.prompt: We finished the storage migration months ago but the old format readers, a compatibility shim and a pile of one-off debug probes are still in the tree. Clean those up for real, but tell me first how you'd prove each one is safe to delete and what you'd keep.
evals.expected_output: Selects the legacy and diagnostics lenses with implementation authorized, requires retirement evidence such as consumer searches or census before deleting, keeps live production diagnostics with a current purpose, and takes no production action to manufacture proof.
assertions: Before deleting an old-format reader or the shim, requires concrete retirement evidence: a read-only census or migration verification showing no old-format data remains, plus traced consumers including restore or rollback paths. The migration's age alone is not proof.
Keeps any probe or diagnostic that still has a live production purpose and removes only leftovers with no current consumer.
Does not propose a production action, such as running a migration or deleting stored data, just to manufacture proof for the source cleanup.
